subject: Geography
central_question: How does geography explain spatial variation and integrate physical and human phenomena to understand the earth as the home of people?
in_scope_units: Purpose, meaning and scope of geography.
Areal differentiation, causal relationships and nature–human interaction.
The questions what, where and why and spatial organisation.
Systematic and regional approaches and branches.
Methods, physical geography and sustainable development.
banned_topics: Detailed Indian boundaries, which belong to India — Location.
Detailed monsoon mechanisms, which belong to Climate.
Detailed landform processes, which belong to Geomorphic Processes.

known_pitfalls.claim: Geography only lists places and physical features.
known_pitfalls.correction: It explains distribution, location, association and causal relationships.

known_pitfalls.claim: Geography belongs only to natural science.
known_pitfalls.correction: It integrates natural and social sciences.

known_pitfalls.claim: What and where are sufficient for scientific geography.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter emphasises why for causal explanation.

known_pitfalls.claim: Systematic and regional approaches are identical.
known_pitfalls.correction: One studies a phenomenon globally; the other studies many phenomena within a region.

known_pitfalls.claim: Physical geography has no human relevance.
known_pitfalls.correction: Landforms, climate, water, soils and ecosystems influence resources and development.

recommended_example_progression: Use Exercise 1(iv) to identify why as the cause–effect question.
Use Exercise 2(i) to decide whether cultural features belong in geography.
Use Exercise 3(i) to explain areal differentiation.
Use Exercise 3(ii) to integrate geography with history, civics and economics.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter contains Exercises 1(i–v), 2(i–v), 3(i–ii), and a three-part Project Work on forests.
